$comment: Every lab validation rule, which validator owns it, and why any rule lives in only one of them. portal/test/validator.test.js and scripts/test_validate_labs.py each fail when their validator's rule ids and this list disagree, so a rule cannot be added to either validator without being recorded here.

validators.js: portal/lib/validator.js (validateLabDir, RULE_IDS). Runs on every generated lab inside generateLab(), on labs/ in portal/test/validator.test.js, and behind the portal's GET /api/validate.
validators.python: validate_labs.py (RULES_BY_CHECK, RULE_IDS). Runs on labs/ in CI, and on an offline lab-builder build through --lab-dir in the same CI job.

rules.checks: The lab directory contains index.md.
index.md has an H1 outside fenced code.
index.md has exactly one H1 outside fenced code: the lab title. Every section heading starts at H2. A '# comment' inside a fenced code sample is code and is not counted.
A heading introduces the lab.
rules.notes: JS accepts an H2-or-deeper heading naming Overview, Introduction, Why this lab, Why ... cares, or About this lab. Python accepts a heading at any level naming Overview or Introduction.

rules.checks: A heading lists what the learner will achieve.
rules.notes: JS accepts an H2-or-deeper heading naming Objective(s) or What you will/you'll learn, do, or build. Python accepts a heading at any level naming Objectives or What you will/you'll learn.

rules.checks: The lab has step headings.
rules.notes: JS accepts any heading after the title that names a step, chapter, part, or use case, or carries a number. Python accepts a heading naming Use Cases, Lab Flow, Step-by-Step, Steps, Step N, Exercise, Walkthrough, Instructions, or Section N.

rules.checks: No TODO, FIXME, TBD, or XXX marker ships to a learner.
rules.notes: JS scans all of index.md, code included, because the composer must never emit one. Python scans every Markdown file in the lab but ignores fenced and inline code, where a marker can be legitimate sample content.

rules.checks: index.md has a pipe-separated metadata table with at least three rows.
rules.asymmetry: The portal catalog reads lab metadata from this table (portal/lib/labs.js), so JS requires the table and each field it reads. Python's has-metadata is a looser presence check kept from the historical validators.

rules.checks: The metadata table has a **DIFFICULTY** value.
rules.asymmetry: Per-field metadata the portal catalog reads; see has-metadata-table.

rules.checks: The metadata table has a **TIME** value.
rules.asymmetry: Per-field metadata the portal catalog reads; see has-metadata-table. Python compares TIME with the README catalog under readme-catalog.

rules.checks: The metadata table has a **PRODUCTS** value.
rules.asymmetry: Per-field metadata the portal catalog reads; see has-metadata-table.

rules.checks: The metadata table has a **TAGS** value.
rules.asymmetry: Per-field metadata the portal catalog reads; see has-metadata-table.

rules.checks: The metadata table has an **INDUSTRY** or **INDUSTRIES** value.
rules.asymmetry: Per-field metadata the portal catalog reads; see has-metadata-table.

rules.checks: index.md has at least 500 characters of content.
rules.asymmetry: Guards against a degenerate composer output, such as a module list that rendered empty. Hand-written labs are far longer; the portal test holds labs/ to it all the same.

rules.checks: Every local image referenced from index.md exists.
rules.asymmetry: Python's no-broken-local-links resolves the same targets, plus anchors, in every Markdown file.

rules.checks: Every relative link in index.md resolves on disk, so a bare documentation slug such as (nlu-boost-node) cannot ship.
rules.asymmetry: Python's no-broken-local-links resolves the same targets, plus anchors, in every Markdown file.

rules.checks: Every heading has body content or a deeper child heading.
rules.asymmetry: Written to catch composer output with a heading and no body. Hand-written labs meet it too, and the portal test holds labs/ to it, so a Python copy would add nothing CI does not already enforce.

rules.checks: Every referenced screenshot or image file exists (reported separately for the portal dashboard).
rules.asymmetry: A dashboard-facing restatement of no-broken-image-refs; Python covers the targets under no-broken-local-links.

rules.checks: Warns when assets/ holds images that index.md never references. Never fails.
rules.asymmetry: A warning for the portal dashboard, not a gate. Python only has pass or fail.

rules.checks: The lab declares metadata: a Metadata heading, a bold DIFFICULTY/TIME/PRODUCTS/TAGS/INDUSTRIES field, or author front matter.
rules.asymmetry: The looser historical presence check. JS enforces the stricter has-metadata-table and per-field rules instead.

rules.checks: A Prerequisites heading.
rules.asymmetry: Carried over from the historical Python validators. Generated labs are held to it by the CI step that runs validate_labs.py --lab-dir on an offline build.

rules.checks: A heading naming Validation, What You Built, Success Criteria, Review, or Verify.
rules.asymmetry: Carried over from the historical Python validators. Generated labs are held to it by the CI step that runs validate_labs.py --lab-dir on an offline build.

rules.checks: A heading naming Summary, Congratulations, Next Steps, Completion, Complete, Conclusion, Wrap-up, or Recap.
rules.asymmetry: Carried over from the historical Python validators. Generated labs are held to it by the CI step that runs validate_labs.py --lab-dir on an offline build.

rules.checks: Every local file, asset, and heading-anchor target in the lab's Markdown resolves. Over labs/ it runs on every tracked Markdown file in the repository.
rules.asymmetry: Python resolves heading anchors and scans every Markdown file. The JS rule set checks only index.md's file targets (no-broken-image-refs, no-broken-relative-links), which is what generateLab() needs before it reports success.

rules.checks: Heading levels never skip, images have meaningful alt text, link text makes sense out of context, and tables have header cells.
rules.asymmetry: Not ported to JS. Generated labs are held to it by the CI step that runs validate_labs.py --lab-dir on an offline build.

rules.checks: README.md lists every lab under labs/ exactly once, with a duration that matches the lab's TIME.
rules.asymmetry: Describes the repository, not a lab. It has no meaning for a generated lab, so --lab-dir does not run it.

rules.checks: No two labs/NN-* folders share a number.
rules.asymmetry: Describes the repository, not a lab. It has no meaning for a generated lab, so --lab-dir does not run it.
